title: Objective Examination
instructions: This paper contains ONE HUNDRED (100) objective questions.
Each question has four options, A to D. Only ONE option is correct.
Circle or shade the letter of the correct option on your answer sheet.

questions.stem: Subject indexing is best defined as:

options.A: The physical binding and shelving of documents
options.B: The process of representing a document's subject content with terms for retrieval
options.C: The process of printing a book's table of contents
options.D: A method of cataloguing authors alphabetically

questions.stem: According to Lancaster (2003), subject indexing involves:

options.A: Assigning a call number to a document
options.B: Translating a document into another language
options.D: Determining subject content and assigning terms that adequately represent it for retrieval

questions.stem: Subject analysis takes place:

options.A: Before index terms are assigned, as the indexer identifies the main topic and concepts
options.B: After index terms have been assigned
options.C: Only when a document is being digitised

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the stated objectives of subject indexing?

options.B: Maximising the number of pages in a document

options.A: A systematically arranged guide to a document's contents, with terms and locators

options.C: A summary of a document written by its author
options.D: A list of a document's illustrations only

questions.stem: A document is considered 'relevant' when it:

questions.stem: Exhaustivity refers to:

options.D: The number of synonyms a thesaurus contains

questions.stem: Specificity refers to:

options.A: The number of index terms assigned to a document
options.B: How precisely an indexing term represents the actual subject of a document
options.C: The physical size of a document
options.D: How quickly a document can be retrieved

options.A: Banned the use of controlled vocabularies

questions.stem: Which of the following is a major indexing and abstracting service?

options.A: Generating entirely new wording not found in the source

questions.stem: Abstractive summarisation attempts to:

options.A: Represent the source's meaning using newly generated wording

questions.stem: In the complete indexing-and-abstracting workflow, indexing mainly provides:

options.A: Structured access points that make a document findable

questions.stem: Automatic indexing uses:

questions.stem: A dynamic index is distinctive because it:
